originalTitle: Xbox revenue drops 10 percent as Microsoft’s cloud and AI business surges

content: Xbox is having yet another tough quarter, as revenue from content and services like its Game Pass subscription dipped 10 percent over the past few months. At the same time, Xbox hardware sales declined 13 percent, according to Microsoft’s fourth-quarter earnings report released on Wednesday. The news comes just weeks after Xbox head Asha Sharma announced a “reset” plan for Xbox that included sweeping layoffs and the spinoff of four games studios, including South of Midnight developer Compulsion Games and Psychonauts creator Double Fine Productions. Sharma has also made some other big changes to Xbox, including lowering GamePass prices, testing free, ad-supported cloud gaming, and making Gears of War: E-Day and Clockwork Revolution Xbox exclusives. Xbox also plans to raise the prices of its consoles by $100 and more starting August 1st. “When it comes to Xbox, we are making the necessary decisions required across our content portfolio, platform, and operations to reset the business for long-term growth,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said during an earnings call. He added that Microsoft expects “to return the business to growth in fiscal 2027.” As Microsoft ramps up efforts in AI, its cloud business has pushed the company’s overall revenue to $90 billion. Microsoft Cloud revenue soared 27 percent to $59.3 billion over the past few months, while revenue from its productivity business, which includes services like Microsoft 365 and LinkedIn, spiked 14 percent to $37.8 billion. Microsoft 365 Copilot also reached more than 30 million paid seats and Azure revenue hit more than $100 billion for the first time. But Xbox wasn’t Microsoft’s only segment on the decline. The company’s Windows OEM and devices segment decreased 7 percent “driven by lower PC market demand.” Microsoft took the wraps off a new Surface device with RTX Spark, Nvidia’s new Arm-based processor in June, and is also starting to make quality-of-life changes to Windows 11 as it aims to regain user trust. Update, July 29th: Added a statement from Satya Nadella.
chineseTitle: 微软云和 AI 业务激增 Xbox 收入下降 10%

chineseContent: Xbox 又经历了一个艰难的季度，其 Game Pass 订阅等内容和服务的收入在过去几个月下降了 10%。与此同时，根据微软周三发布的第四季度财报，Xbox 硬件销量下降了 13%。就在几周前，Xbox 负责人阿莎·夏尔马 (Asha Sharma) 宣布了 Xbox 的“重置”计划，其中包括大规模裁员和分拆四家游戏工作室，其中包括《South of Midnight》开发商 Compulsion Games 和《Psychonauts》开发商 Double Fine Productions。 Sharma 还对 Xbox 做出了一些其他重大改变，包括降低 GamePass 价格、免费测试、支持广告的云游戏，以及将《战争机器：E-Day》和《发条革命》制作为 Xbox 独占游戏。 Xbox 还计划从 8 月 1 日起将其游戏机的价格提高 100 美元甚至更多。微软首席执行官萨提亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 在财报电话会议上表示：“就 Xbox 而言，我们正在内容组合、平台和运营方面做出必要的决策，以重新调整业务以实现长期增长。”他补充说，微软预计“到 2027 财年业务将恢复增长”。随着微软在人工智能方面加大力度，其云业务已将公司整体收入推至900亿美元。过去几个月，微软云收入飙升 27% 至 593 亿美元，而包括 Microsoft 365 和 LinkedIn 等服务在内的生产力业务收入飙升 14% 至 378 亿美元。 Microsoft 365 Copilot 的付费席位也超过 3000 万，Azure 收入首次突破 1000 亿美元。但 Xbox 并不是微软唯一下滑的细分市场。 “由于 PC 市场需求下降，该公司的 Windows OEM 和设备部门下降了 7%”
